mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand and earnings pressure, which reduces corporate profit growth and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0 and remains above for at least two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where UNRATE > 5% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals deteriorating demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity and lower corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods of three consecutive monthly INDPRO declines (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 135,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market growth, which supports consumer demand and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 135,000 and remains above for at least three months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods where PAYEMS > 135,000 for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals strengthening demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline in periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 rises (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with weakening manufacturing activity, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% and remains above for at least three months AND INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months and INDPRO declines for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
